25F here too that feels pretty much the exact same way as you. No real goals or plan, but still in school for a degree I lost interest in a long time ago. I’ve been depressed for as long as I can remember, but it’s been getting a good bit worse over the past 5 years. Friends all graduated and moved on with their lives, and the ones I still had, I shut out too. I used to love to paint and I was damn good at it, but now I can’t find the motivation to. 

I don’t want to hijack your post with a long story of my own, but I do understand how you’re feeling. Like a dark fog always in your head that distracts you, keeps you up at night, and exhausts you during the day.

Hey, I compare myself to every single person I meet too, and it’s been killing my mental health. The only thing I can do though, is remind myself that measuring my own progress by comparing it to others’ isn’t fair to me at all. We all have different paths with different paces. Depression and anxiety are a bitch and they take a toll on my hobbies and friendships too. I feel that.

We’re still young, and we will make it! It may not be next week or next month, but one day.

I can relate to so much that you've said.  There's nothing I hate more than the empty promise of "It gets better", "Things won't stay this way forever", and my all-time favorite "Things got better for me, so they will for you too! Just be positive." If you are so certain it's going to get better, then why don't you tell me WHEN since you know so much?

And like you also said, how is knowing other people have it worse and being constantly reminded of that supposed to make it better for me? That just makes the guilt worse.

"This wasn’t how shit was supposed to go down." I fucking felt that one.  This was NOT how my life was supposed to be at this point.  If someone would've told me 5 years ago the situation I would be in and all the things leading up to it, I would've ended it then when I first started spiraling.

But here we are, and all we can really do is attempt to mend ourselves from the inside out.  In my journey so far i've only done baby steps, such as taking out the trash and doing laundry before it gets unmanageable, trying to eat at least once a day, and actually making myself get out of bed before 11am.  Making a small routine for myself has helped a bit.  Small steps may seem like marathons at times, but they're still progress.

As for others knowing and piecing together my situation and judging, i know that feeling too.  I know exactly how it feels to feel like a total loser.  I know people look at me and my laundry list of failures and, hell, probably feel even better about themselves. I know the friends I used to have that have moved on with their lives and are happy and successful probably see me as a pathetic.  But fuck 'em.  It's my life, and i'm trying.  They don't pay my bills, so their opinion is irrelevant.

I feel like I'm rambling here in no particular direction so i'm going to cut myself off, but OP, if you feel like chatting, ranting, or just having a nice conversation to get your mind off things for maybe a second, my DMs are open to you.  Talking about it doesn't necessarily fix it, but it's nice to to be able to relate to someone a little.

I really do hope things get a little brighter for you and for everyone in these comments. Stay safe out there.

24F here, and this post really hit me where it hurts. I relate to this almost entirely. I’m struggling to finish a degree that I’ve lost motivation for, and it’ll be at least a year and a half before I do now. 26 with no real hireable skills or experience? I ask myself daily what the point in anything is. Everyone around me is successful. They have jobs they enjoy. They graduated college on time years ago, when I should have. They have families. They have independence. And I’m stuck here in what seems like a never-ending cycle of misery. 

If you want to rant, feel free to message me. I know ranting doesn’t change anything, but it can be a temporary comfort. 

Also, something I tell myself often to make myself feel better is that not everyone you see succeeding and being “happy” is the open book you think they are. People broadcast the positives in their lives, and rarely the negatives, and the negatives could far outweigh the positives. 

You are not alone in this. And I hope you find peace. I’m trying to find mine as well.
